location: Port of Long Beach, Pier G
description: Severe vessel backlog caused by dual gantry crane power failures and chassis shortages during peak holiday volume. Over 28 container ships waited at anchorage with average berthing delays exceeding 4 days.
mitigation_outcome: Diverted secondary feeder vessels to Oakland terminal; rerouted urgent refrigerated cargo via air freight to minimize perishable spoilage.

description: Warning strikes by union workers ground all vessel loading and unloading operations to a complete standstill across the Elbe river terminals for 48 consecutive hours.
mitigation_outcome: Carriers declared force majeure, held export containers at inland rail hubs in Munich and Nuremberg, and rescheduled feeder rotations.

location: South China Sea / Yantian Port, Shenzhen
description: Super Typhoon Malakas forced mandatory port evacuation, suspension of gate-in procedures for dry and reefer containers, and channel navigation closures.
mitigation_outcome: Vessels adjusted cruising speed to wait out the storm system in open waters; port restarted gate operations on a prioritized queue 12 hours after storm warnings subsided.

event_type: Canal Transit Bottleneck / Low Water Levels
description: Prolonged drought led the Canal Authority to cut daily booking slots by 35% and enforce strict maximum draft limits of 44 feet on Neo-Panamax vessels.
mitigation_outcome: Carriers rerouted non-urgent East Coast bulk shipments via the Suez Canal and Cape of Good Hope, absorbing 10 additional transit days.

description: Intermodal freight train derailment blocked main arterial classification tracks, delaying intermodal container transfers heading toward Midwest distribution centers.
mitigation_outcome: Cargo was transferred to local drayage trucks for expedited cross-docking; main track was cleared within 28 hours.
